entries.lyrics: Christ Je-sus lay in death's strong bands, For our of-fen-ses_ giv-en; But now at God's right hand He stands, And brings us life from_ Hea-ven. Where-fore let us joy-ful be, And sing to God right thank-ful-ly Loud songs of Al-le-lu__-ia! Al-le_-lu-ia!

entries.title: Come Forth! Come on, with Solemn Song!

entries.lyrics: Come forth! come on, with sol-emn song! The road is short, the rest is long! The Lord brought here, He calls a-way: Make no de-lay, This home was for a pas-sing day.

entries.title: Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing

entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune NETTLETON (American folk hymn); words by Robert Robinson (1735–1790).
entries.lyrics: Come, Thou Fount of ev-ery bless-ing, Tune my heart to sing Thy grace; Streams of mer-cy, ne-ver ceas-ing, Call for songs of loud-est praise. Teach me_ some me-lo-dious son_-net, Sung by_ fla-ming tongues a-bove; Praise the mount! I’m fixed u-pon it, Mount of Thy re-deem-ing love.

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune JEFFERSON (From Southern Harmony, 1835); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).
entries.lyrics: Come, Thou_ long ex_-pect-ed_ Je-sus Born_ to_ set Thy_ peo-ple free; From our_ fears and_ sins re_-lease us, Let_ us_ find our_ rest in Thee. Is-rael's Strength and Con-sol_-a-tion, Hope of all the_ earth Thou_ art; Dear De_-sire of ev-ery_ na-tion, Joy_ of_ ev-ery_ long-ing heart.

entries.title: Come, Ye Disconsolate
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune CONSOLATOR (WEBBE) by Samuel Webbe (1740–1816); words by Thomas Moore (1779–1852) and Thomas Hastings (1784–1872).
entries.lyrics: Come, ye dis-con-so-late, wher_-'er ye lan-guish; Come to the mer-cy seat, fer-vent-ly kneel. Here bring your woun-ded hearts, here tell_ your_ an-guish; Earth_ has no sor-row that Heav'n can-not heal.

entries.title: Come, Ye Thankful People, Come
entries.source: the score on the tune's Wikipedia article (melody and underlay), which matches the tune as it is sung; not in the Open Hymnal.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune ST GEORGE’S WINDSOR by George Job Elvey (1816–1893); words by Henry Alford (1810–1871).
entries.lyrics: Come, ye thank-ful peo-ple, come, Raise the song of har-vest home: All is safe-ly gath-ered in, Ere the win-ter storms be-gin; God, our Mak-er, doth pro-vide For our wants to be sup-plied: Come to God’s own tem-ple, come, Raise the song of har-vest home.

entries.title: Comfort, Comfort Ye My People

entries.lyrics: Com-fort, com-fort ye My peo-ple, Speak ye peace, thus saith our God; Com-fort those who sit in dark-ness, Mourn-ing 'neath their sor-row's load; Speak ye to Je-ru-sa-lem Of the peace that waits for them; Tell her that her sins I co-ver, And her war-fare now is o-ver.

entries.title: Creator of the Stars of Night (Conditor Alme Siderum)

entries.lyrics: Cre-a-tor of the stars of night, Thy peo-ple's ev-er-las-ting light, Je-su, Re-dee-mer, save us all, And hear Thy ser-vants when they call.

entries.lyrics: Cre-a-tor of the stars of night, Thy peo-ple's ev-er-las-ting light, Je-su, Re-dee-mer, save us all, And hear Thy ser-vants when they call.

entries.title: Crown Him with Many Crowns
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Appendix to Hymns Ancient and Modern, 1869); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.

entries.credit: Tune DIADEMATA by George Job Elvey (1816–1893); words by Matthew Bridges (1800–1894).
entries.lyrics: Crown Him with man-y crowns, The Lamb up-on His throne; Hark! how the heav’n-ly an-them_ drowns All mu-sic but its own: A-wake, my soul, and sing Of Him who died for thee, And hail Him as thy match-less King Through all e-ter-ni-ty.

entries.title: Day of Wrath, O Day of Mourning
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.

entries.lyrics: Day of wrath, O day of mourn-ing! See ful-filled the pro-phet's warn-ing, Heav'n and earth in ash-es burn-ing. Oh, what fear man's bo-som rend-eth When from Heav'n the Judge de-scend-eth On whose sen-tence all de-pend_-eth!

entries.title: Dear Christians, One and All Rejoice (Es Ist Gewisslich an Der Zeit)

entries.lyrics: Dear Christ-ians, one and all re-joice, With ex-ul-ta-tion spring-ing, And with u-ni-ted heart and voice And ho-ly rap-ture sing-ing, Pro-claim the won-ders God hath done, How his right arm the vic-t'ry won; Right dear-ly it hath cost him.

entries.lyrics: Dear Christ-ians, one and all re-joice, With ex-ul-ta-tion spring_-ing, And with u-ni-ted heart and voice And ho-ly rap-ture sing_-ing, Pro-claim the won-ders God hath done, How his right arm the vic-t'ry won; Right dear-ly it hath cost_ him.

entries.title: Did You Think to Pray?
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune STOCKBRIDGE by William Oscar Perkins (1831–1902); words by Mary Ann Pepper Kidder (1820–1905).
entries.lyrics: Ere you left your room this morn-ing, Did you think to pray? In the name of Christ our Sa-vior, Did you sue for lov-ing fa-vor, As a shield to-day? O how pray-ing rests the wea-ry! Prayer will change the night to day; So when life seems dark and drea-ry, Don't for-get to pray.

entries.title: Evening and Morning
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DIE GÜLDNE SONNE by Johann Georg Ebeling (1637–1676); words by Paul Gerhardt (1607–1676); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: Eve-ning and mor_-ning, Sun-set and daw_-ning, Wealth, peace, and glad-ness, Com-fort in sad-ness, These are Thy works; all the glo-ry be Thine! Times wi-thout num-ber, A-wake or in slum-ber, Thine eye ob-serves us, From dan-ger pre-serves us, Cau-sing Thy mer-cy u-pon us to shine.

entries.title: Every Morning Mercies New
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune KELSO by Edward John Hopkins (1818–1901); words by Greville Phillimore (1821–1884).
entries.lyrics: Ev-'ry morn-ing mer-cies new Fall as fresh as morn-ing dew; Ev-'ry morn-ing let us pay Tri-bute_ with the ear-ly day: For Thy mer-cies, Lord, are sure; Thy com-pas-sion doth en-dure.

entries.lyrics: Faith of our fa_-thers, liv_-ing still, In spite of dun-geon, fi-re and sword; O how our hearts_ beat high_ with joy When-e'er we hear that glo_-rious Word! Faith of our fa-thers, ho-ly faith! We will be true to thee till death.

entries.lyrics: Far, far a-way on Ju-de-a's_ plains, Shep-herds of old heard the joy_-ous_ strains:_ Glo-ry to God, glo-ry to God, Glo-ry to God in the high_-est; Peace on earth, good will to men; Peace on earth, good will to men.

entries.title: For the Beauty of the Earth
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score; every note and the underlay agree with the score on Wikipedia's article, and the opening with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune DIX by Conrad Kocher (1786–1872) and William Henry Monk (1823–1889); words by Folliott Sandford Pierpoint (1835–1917).
entries.lyrics: For the_ beau-ty of the earth, For the glo-ry of the skies, For the_ love which from our birth O-ver and a-round us lies: Lord of all, to Thee we raise This our hymn of grate-ful praise.

entries.title: From God Shall Naught Divide Me
entries.tune: VON GOTT WILL ICH NICHT LASSEN
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.

entries.lyrics: From God shall naught di-vide me, For He is true for aye, And on my path will guide me, Who else should of-ten stray; His e-ver boun-teous hand By night and day is heed-ful And gives me what is need-ful, Wher-e'er I go or stand.

entries.title: From Heaven Above to Earth I Come

entries.lyrics: From Heaven a-bove to earth I come, To bear good news to ev-ery home; Glad ti-dings of great joy I bring, Where-of I now will say_ and sing.

entries.title: From Nazareth

entries.lyrics: Comes a-ny good from Na-za-reth? The scorn-ful cha_-llenge as of old Is flung on man-y'a jeer-ing breath From cloi-stered cells and marts of gold.

entries.title: Gentle Mary Laid Her Child
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune TEMPUS ADEST FLORIDUM (From Swedish Piae Cantones, 1582); words by Joseph Simpson Cook (1859–1933).
entries.lyrics: Gen-tle Ma-ry laid her Child low-ly in a man-ger; There He lay, the un-de-filed, to the world a Stran-ger: Such a Babe in such a place, can He be the Sa-vior? Ask the saved of all the race who have found His fa_-vor.

entries.title: Glorious Things of Thee Are Spoken
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score and the score on Wikipedia's article, which agree on every note and on the underlay.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune AUSTRIA by Joseph Haydn (1732–1809); words by John Newton (1725–1807).
entries.lyrics: Glo-rious things of thee are spo_-ken, Zi-on, cit-y of our_ God; He whose word can-not be bro_-ken Formed thee for His own a_-bode: On the Rock_ of A-ges found_-ed, What can shake thy sure re-pose? With sal-va-tion’s walls sur-round_-ed, Thou may’st_ smile_ at_ all thy_ foes.

entries.title: Go to Dark Gethsemane

entries.lyrics: Go to dark Geth-se-ma-ne, ye that feel the temp-ter's pow'r; Your Re-deem-er's con-flict see, watch with Him one bit-ter hour, Turn not from His griefs a-way; learn from Je-sus Christ to pray.

entries.title: God Bless Our Native Land

entries.lyrics: God bless our na-tive land! Firm may she e-ver stand Through storm and night; When the wild tem-pests rave, Ru-ler of wind and wave, Do Thou_ our_ coun-try save By_ Thy great might.

entries.title: God Himself Is Present
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WUNDERBARER KÖNIG by Joachim Neander (1650–1680); words by Gerhard Tersteegen (1697–1769); translated by Frederick William Foster (1760–1835) and John Miller (1756–1790).
entries.lyrics: God Him-self is pre-sent: Let us now a-dore Him, And with awe ap-pear be-fore Him. God is in His tem-ple, all with-in keep si-lence, Pro-strate lie with deep-est rev-erence. Him a-lone God we own, Him our God and Sa-vior; Praise His name for-ev-er.

entries.title: God, That Madest Earth and Heaven
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.

entries.lyrics: God, that ma-dest earth and Hea-ven, dark-ness and light; Who the day for toil hast giv-en, for rest the night; May Thine an-gel guards de-fend us, Slum-ber sweet Thy mer-cy send us; Ho-ly dreams and hopes at-tend us, all through the night.

entries.lyrics: God, whose al-might_-y word Cha-os and dark__-ness heard And took their flight: Hear us, we hum-ble pray, And where the Gos-pel day Sheds not its glor-ious ray, Let there be light!

entries.title: God Will Take Care of You
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune MARTIN by Walter Stillman Martin (1862–1935); words by Civilla Durfee Martin (1866–1948).
entries.lyrics: Be not dis-mayed_ what-e'er be-tide, God will take care of you;_ Be-neath His wings_ of love a-bide, God will take care of you. God will take care of you, through ev-'ry day, o'er all the way; He will take care_ of you, God will take care_ of you.

entries.title: Good King Wenceslas
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune TEMPUS ADEST FLORIDUM (traditional spring carol); words by John Mason Neale (1818–1866).
entries.lyrics: Good King Wen-ces-las looked out On the feast of Ste-phen, When the snow lay round a-bout, Deep and crisp and e-ven; Bright-ly shone the moon that night, Though the frost was cru-el, When a poor man came in sight, Gath-’ring win-ter fu_-el.

entries.title: Guide Me, O Thou Great Jehovah
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (The Methodist Hymn Book, 1933); every note agrees with the score on Wikipedia's Cwm Rhondda article (printed there in 4/2 in A flat) and the opening with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune CWM RHONDDA by John Hughes (1873–1932); words by William Williams (1717–1791) and Peter Williams (1723–1796).
entries.lyrics: Guide me, O Thou great_ Je_-ho-vah, Pil-grim through this bar-ren land; I am weak, but Thou_ art_ might-y; Hold me with Thy_ pow’r-ful hand: Bread of heav-en, bread of heav-en, Feed me till I want no more; Feed me till_ I_ want no more.

entries.lyrics: Man of Sor-rows! what a name For the Son of God, who came Ru-ined sin-ners to re-claim. Hal-le-lu-jah! What a Sa-vior!

entries.lyrics: Hap-py the man who fear-eth God, Whose feet His ho-ly ways have trod; Thine own good hand shall nour-ish thee, And well and hap-py shalt_ thou be.

entries.lyrics: Hap-py the man who fear_-eth God, Whose feet His ho-ly ways_ have trod; Thine own good hand_ shall nour-ish thee, And well and hap-py shalt____ thou be.

entries.title: Hark the Glad Sound

entries.lyrics: Hark, the glad sound! the Sa_-vior comes! The Sa_-vior pro_-mised long; Let ev_-ery heart_ pre-pare_ a throne, And ev_-ery voice_ a song.

entries.lyrics: Hark! the her-ald an-gels sing_ Glo-ry to the new-born King; Peace on earth, and mer-cy mild,_ God and sin-ners re-con-ciled! Joy-ful, all ye na-tions, rise,_ Join the tri-umph of the skies;_ With th’an-gel-ic host pro-claim, Christ is_ born in Beth-le-hem! Hark! the her-ald an-gels sing Glo-ry_ to the new-born King.

entries.title: Hark the Sound of Holy Voices
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune O DURCHBRECHER by Johann Anastasius Freylinghausen (1670–1739); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: Hark the sound of ho-ly voi-ces, chan-ting at the crys-tal sea Hal-le-lu-ia! Hal-le-lu-ia! Hal-le-lu-ia! Lord to Thee. Mul-ti-tude which none can num-ber, like the stars in glo-ry stand Clothed in white ap-pa-rel, hol-ding palms of vic-t'ry in their hand.

entries.title: Hark, the Voice of Jesus Calling

entries.lyrics: There's with-in my heart a mel-o-dy Je-sus whis-pers sweet and low,_ "Fear not, I am with thee, peace, be still," In all of life's ebb and flow. Je-sus, Je-sus, Je-sus,‑ Sweet-est name I know, Fills my ev-'ry long-ing, Keeps me sing-ing as I go.

He lead-eth me, He lead-eth_ me, By His own hand_ He_ lead-eth me; His faith-ful fol-low'r I would_ be, For by His hand_ He_ lead-eth me.

entries.lyrics: "He was not will-ing that a-ny should per-ish"; Je-sus en-throned in the glo-ry a-bove, Saw our poor fal-len world, pi-tied our sor-rows, Poured out His life for us, won-der-ful love! Per-ish-ing, per-ish-ing! Throng-ing our path-way, Hearts break with bur-dens too hea-vy to bear: Je-sus would save, but there's no one to tell them, No one to lift them from sin and des-pair.

entries.lyrics: He_ who would val_-iant be 'gainst all dis-a-ster, Let_ him in con_-stan-cy fol-low the Mas-ter. There's no dis-cour-age_-ment shall make_ him once re-lent His first a-vowed_ in_-tent to be a pil-grim.

entries.lyrics: Heav'n-ly Fa-ther, send Thy bles-sing On Thy chil-dren ga-thered here, May they all, Thy Name con-fes-sing, Be to Thee fo-re-ver dear; May they be, like Jo-seph, lo-ving, Du-ti-ful, and chaste, and pure; And their faith, like Da-vid, pro-ving, Stead-fast un-to death en-dure.

entries.lyrics: Ho-ly Ghost, with light di-vine Shine up-on this heart of mine; Chase the shades of night a-way, Turn the_ dark-ness in-to day.

entries.lyrics: Ho-ly God,_ we praise_ Thy Name; Lord of all,_ we bow_ be-fore Thee! All on earth_ Thy scep_-ter claim, All in Hea-ven a-bove_ a-dore Thee; In-fin_-ite_ Thy vast do_-main, Ev-er-last_-ing is_ Thy reign.

entries.lyrics: Ho-ly, ho-ly, ho-ly! Lord God Al-might-y! Ear-ly in the morn-ing our song shall rise to Thee; Ho-ly, ho-ly, ho-ly! mer-ci-ful and might-y, God in three Per-sons, bless-ed Trin-i-ty!

entries.lyrics: Ho-san-na,_ loud ho-san_-na, the lit_-tle child-ren sang; Through pil-lared_ court and tem_-ple the love_-ly an-them rang. To_ Je-sus, Who had blessed__ them close_ fold-ed to His breast, The child-ren_ sang their prais_-es, the simp_-lest and the best.

entries.title: How Blest the Hearts

entries.lyrics: How blest are hearts, which Christ the Lord Cou-ples as with a sil-ver cord, In nu-ptial u-ni-ty: That a-ni-ma-ted are by love And a-spi-ra-tions from a-bove, O Ho-ly Ghost, by Thee!

entries.title: How Can I Keep from Singing?
entries.tune: HOW CAN I KEEP FROM SINGING
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HOW CAN I KEEP FROM SINGING by Robert Lowry (1826–1899); words by F. J. Hartley (1845–1922), Robert Lowry (1826–1899) and Anonymous.
entries.lyrics: My life flows on in end-less song; A-bove earth's la-men-ta-tion. I catch the sweet, though far-off hymn that hails a new cre-a-tion; Through all the tu-mult and the strife, I hear that mu-sic ring-ing; It finds an e-cho in my soul... How can I keep from sing-ing?

entries.title: How Firm a Foundation

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune FOUNDATION (FUNK) by Joseph Funk (1778–1862); words by John Rippon (1751–1836).
entries.lyrics: How_ firm a foun-da-tion, ye saints of the Lord, Is laid for your faith in His ex-cel-lent Word! What more can He say than to you He hath said, You, who un-to Je-sus for re-fuge have fled?

entries.title: I Heard the Bells on Christmas Day

entries.lyrics: I heard the bells on Christ-mas day Their old fa-mil-iar car-ols play, And wild and sweet the words re-peat Of peace on earth, good will to men.

entries.title: I Know That My Redeemer Lives

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DUKE STREET by John Hatton (1710–1793); words by Samuel Medley (1738–1799).
entries.lyrics: I know that my Re_-deem-er_ lives; What com-fort this sweet sen-tence gives! He lives, He lives,_ who_ once_ was_ dead; He lives, my ev-er liv-ing Head.

entries.title: I Know Whom I Have Believed
entries.tune: I KNOW WHOM I HAVE BELIEVED
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune I KNOW WHOM I HAVE BELIEVED by James McGranahan (1840–1907); words by Daniel Webster Whittle (1840–1901) and Elias Nathan (1840–1901).
entries.lyrics: I know not why_ God's_ won-drous grace To me He hath_ made_ known, Nor why, un-wor_-thy,_ Christ in love Re-deemed me for_ His_ own. But I know Whom I have be-liev-èd, And am per-sua-ded that He is ab-le To keep that which I've com-mit-ted Un-to Him a-gainst that day.

entries.title: I Need Thee Every Hour
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Pentecostal Hymns No. 2, 1898); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune NEED by Robert Lowry (1826–1899); words by Annie Sherwood Hawks (1835–1918) and Robert Lowry (1826–1899).
entries.lyrics: I need Thee ev-’ry hour, Most gra_-cious_ Lord; No ten-der voice like Thine Can peace_ af_-ford. I need Thee, O I need Thee; Ev-’ry hour I need Thee; O bless me now, my Sav-iour, I come_ to Thee!

entries.title: I Sing the Mighty Power of God
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ELLACOMBE (From Gesangbuch der Herzogl. Hofkapelle, Wurttemberg, 1784); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748).
entries.lyrics: I sing the_ migh-ty pow'r of God, That made_ the moun-tains rise; That spread the_ flow-ing seas a-broad, And built_ the lof-ty skies. I_ sing the wis-dom that or_-dained The_ sun to rule the day: The moon shines_ full at His com-mand, And all_ the stars o-bey.

entries.title: I Walk in Danger All the Way

entries.lyrics: I walk in dan-ger all the way; The thought shall ne-ver leave me That Sa-tan, who has marked his prey, Is plot-ting to de-ceive me. This foe with hid-den snares May seize me un-a-wares If e'er I fail to watch and pray: I walk in dan-ger all the way.

entries.title: If God Himself Be for Me
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WOODBIRD (traditional German); words by Paul Gerhardt (1607–1676); translated by Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: If God Him-self be for_ me, I may a host de-fy; For when I pray, be-fore_ me My foes, con-found-ed, fly. If Christ, my Head_ and Mas-ter, Be-friend me from a-bove, What foe or what dis-as_-ter Can drive me from His love?

entries.title: I'm but a Stranger Here
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. EDMUND (SULLIVAN) by Arthur Seymour Sullivan (1842–1900); words by Thomas Rawson Taylor (1807–1835).
entries.lyrics: I'm but a stran-ger here, Heav'n is my home; Earth is a des-ert drear, Heav'n is my home. Dan-ger and sor-row stand round me on ev-ery hand; Heav'n is my fa-ther-land,_ Heav'n is my home.

entries.title: Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (The Hymnal 1940); the harmony in the same source confirms each melody note.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune ST DENIO (Welsh melody); words by Walter Chalmers Smith (1824–1908).
entries.lyrics: Im-mor-tal, in-vis-i-ble, God on-ly wise, In light in-ac-ces-si-ble hid from our eyes, Most bless-ed, most glo-rious, the An-cient of Days, Al-might-y, vic-to-rious, Thy great name we praise.

entries.title: In Peace and Joy I Now Depart
entries.tune: MIT FRIED UND FREUD ICH FAR DAHIN

entries.lyrics: In peace and joy I now de-part At God's dis-pos__-ing; For full of com-fort is_ my heart, Soft re-pos_-ing. So_ the Lord_ hath pro_-mised me, And death is but a slum__-ber.

entries.title: In These Our Days So Perilous

entries.lyrics: In these our days so per-il-ous, Lord, peace in mer-cy send us; No God but Thee can fight for_ us, No God but Thee_ de-fend_ us; Thou our_ on-ly God and_ Sa_-vior.

entries.title: It Came upon a Midnight Clear

entries.lyrics: It came up-on_ the mid-night clear, That glor_-ious song_ of old, From an-gels bend_-ing near the earth, To touch their harps_ of gold; "Peace on the earth,_ good will to men, From Heav-en's all gra_-cious King." The world in so_-lemn still-ness lay, To hear the an_-gels sing.

entries.title: It Is Well with My Soul
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (The Evangelical Hymnal, 1921); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune VILLE DU HAVRE by Philip Paul Bliss (1838–1876); words by Horatio G. Spafford (1828–1888).
entries.lyrics: When peace, like a riv-er, at-tend_-eth my way, When sor-rows like sea bil-lows roll; What-ev-er my lot, Thou hast taught me to say, It is well, it is well with my soul. It is well with my soul, It is well, it is well with my soul.

entries.title: Jerusalem the Golden

entries.lyrics: Jer-u-sa-lem the gol-den, with milk and hon-ey blest, Be-neath thy con-tem-pla-tion sink heart and voice op-pressed. I know not, O I know not, what joys a-wait us there, What ra-dian-cy of glo-ry, what bliss be-yond com-pare.

entries.lyrics: Je-sus came, the heav'ns a-dor-ing, Came with peace from realms on high; Je-sus came for man's re-demp-tion, Low-ly came on earth to die. Al-le-lu-ia!_ Al-le-lu-ia! Came in_ deep hu-mil-i-ty.

entries.lyrics: Je-sus Christ is ris’n to-day,_ Al____-le_-lu_-ia! Our tri-um-phant ho-ly day,_ Al____-le_-lu_-ia! Who did once up-on the cross Al____-le_-lu_-ia! Suf_-fer_ to re-deem our loss._ Al_____-le_-lu_-ia!

entries.lyrics: Je-sus Christ, who came to save,__ And o-ver-came the grave, Is now_ a-ris_-en, And sin hath bound in pri_-son. Ky-ri' e-lei_-son.

entries.title: Jesus, in Thy Dying Woes
entries.tune: WORDS ON THE CROSS - THE LITANY

entries.lyrics: Je-sus, in Thy dy-ing woes, E-ven while Thy life-blood flows, Cra-ving par-don for Thy foes; Hear us, ho-ly Je-sus.

entries.title: Jesus Is All the World to Me
entries.tune: JESUS IS ALL THE WORLD TO ME
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune JESUS IS ALL THE WORLD TO ME by Will Lamartine Thompson (1847–1909); words by Will Lamartine Thompson (1847–1909).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus is all the world to me, My life, my joy, my all; He is my strength from day to day, With-out Him I_ would fall. When I am sad, to Him I go, No o-ther one can cheer me so; When I am sad, He makes me glad, He's my friend.

entries.title: Jesus, King of Glory
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. ALBAN by Franz Joseph Haydn (1732–1809); words by W. Hope Davison (1827–1894).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus, King of glo-ry, throned a-bove the sky, Je-sus, ten-der Sa-vior, hear Thy child-ren cry. Par-don our trans-gres-sions, cleanse us from our sin,_ By Thy Spi-rit help us heav'n-ly life to win. Je-sus, King of glo-ry, throned a-bove the sky, Je-sus, ten-der Sa-vior, hear Thy child-ren cry.

entries.title: Jesus Loves Me
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Bradbury's Golden Chain and Shower, 1866); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.

entries.credit: Tune JESUS LOVES ME by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by Anna Bartlett Warner (1827–1915) and William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus loves me! this I know, For the Bi-ble tells me so; Lit-tle ones to Him be-long; They are weak, but He is strong. Yes, Je-sus loves me! Yes, Je-sus loves me! Yes, Je-sus loves me! The Bi-ble tells me so.

entries.title: Jesus Shall Reign

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DUKE STREET by John Hatton (1710–1793); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus shall reign wher_-e'er the_ sun Does his suc-ces-sive jour-neys run; His king-dom stretch_ from_ shore_ to_ shore Till moons shall wax and wane no more.

entries.title: Jesus, Tender Shepherd, Hear Me
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune EVENING PRAYER by John Stainer (1840–1901); words by Mary Lundie Duncan (1814–1840).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus, ten-der Shep-herd, hear me; Bless Thy lit-tle la-mb to-night; Through the dark-ness be Thou near me; Watch my sleep till morn-ing light.

entries.title: Joy to the World
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ANTIOCH by George Frederick Handel (1685–1759); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748).
entries.lyrics: Joy to the world, the Lord is come! Let earth re-ceive her King; Let ev_-'ry_ heart__ pre-pare_ Him_ room,__ And Heav'n and na-ture_ sing, And_ Heav'n and na-ture_ sing, And_ Heav'n,_ and Heav'n,__ and na-ture sing.

entries.title: Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune HYMN TO JOY by Ludwig van Beethoven (1770–1827) and Edward Hodges (1796–1867); words by Henry van Dyke (1852–1933).
entries.lyrics: Joy-ful, joy-ful, we a-dore thee, God of glo-ry, Lord of love; Hearts un-fold like flowers be-fore thee, Op’-ning to the sun a-bove. Melt the clouds of sin and_ sad-ness; Drive the_ dark of doubt a-way; Giv-er of im-mor-tal glad-ness, Fill us with the light of day!

entries.title: Just as I Am Without One Plea

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WOODWORTH by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by Charlotte Elliott (1789–1871).

entries.lyrics: O come, all ye faith-ful, joy-ful and tri-um-phant, O come ye, O come_ ye to Beth_-le-hem; Come and be-hold Him, born the King of an_-gels: O come, let us a-dore Him, O come, let us a-dore Him, O come, let us a-dore Him,_ Christ_ the Lord.

entries.lyrics: O come, O come, Em-man__-u-el, And ran-som cap-tive Is__-ra-el, That mourns in lone-ly e_-xile here Un-til the Son of God__ ap-pear. Re-joice! Re-joice! Em-man__-u-el shall come to thee, O I__-sra-el.

entries.title: O Day of Rest and Gladness

entries.lyrics: O day of rest and glad_-ness, o day of joy and light, O balm of care and sad_-ness, most beau-ti-ful, most bright: On thee, the high_ and low-ly, through a-ges joined in tune, Sing ho-ly, ho-ly, h_-oly, to the great God Tri-une.

entries.title: O Father, All Creating

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune AURELIA by Samuel Sebastian Wesley (1810–1876); words by John Ellerton (1826–1893).
entries.lyrics: O Fa-ther, all cre-a-ting, Whose wis-dom, love, and pow'r First bound two lives to-ge-ther In E-den's pri-mal hour, To-day to these Thy child-ren Thy ear-liest gifts re-new: A home by Thee made hap-py, A love by Thee kept true.

entries.title: O for a Thousand Tongues

entries.lyrics: O for a thou-sand tongues to sing My great Re-deem-er's praise, The glo-ries of my God and King, The_ tri-umphs of His grace!

entries.credit: Tune ST ANNE by William Croft (1678–1727); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748) and John Wesley (1703–1791).
entries.lyrics: O God, our help in a-ges past, Our hope for years to come, Our shel-ter from the storm-y blast, And our e-ter-nal home.

entries.title: O Grieve Not So, nor So Lament

entries.lyrics: O grieve not so, nor so la-ment, My soul! nor trou-bled sigh, Be-cause some joys to o-thers sent Your Fa-ther may de-ny; Take all as love that seems se-vere There is no want if God is near.

entries.title: O Holy, Blessed Trinity

entries.lyrics: O Ho-ly, Bless-ed Trin-i-ty, Di-vine, Es-sen-tial U-ni-ty, God Fa-ther, Son, and Ho-ly Ghost, Be Thou this day my Guide and Host.

entries.title: O Holy Spirit, Enter in
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WIE SCHÖN LEUCHTET by Phillipp Nicolai (1556–1608); words by Michael Schirmer (1606–1673); translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: O Ho-ly Spir-it, en-ter in, And in our hearts Thy work be-gin Thy Tem-ple deign to make us; Sun of the soul, Thou Light di-vine, A-round and in us bright-ly shine, To joy and glad-ness wake us. That we to Thee Tru-ly liv-ing, To Thee giv-ing Prayer un-ceas-ing May in love be still in-creas-ing.

entries.title: O Little Town of Bethlehem
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. LOUIS by Lewis Henry Redner (1830–1908); words by Phillips Brooks (1835–1893).
entries.lyrics: O lit-tle town of Beth-le-hem, how still we_ see thee lie! A-bove thy deep and dream-less sleep the si-lent_ stars go by. Yet in thy dark streets shin-eth the ev-er-last-ing Light; The hopes and fears of all the years are met in thee to-night.

entries.title: O Lord, How Shall I Meet Thee
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WIE SOLL ICH DICH EMPFANGE by Johann Crüger (1598–1662); words by Paul Gerhardt (1607–1676); translated by Anonymous.
entries.lyrics: O Lord, how shall I meet Thee, How wel-come Thee a-right? All na-tions long to see Thee, My Hope, my heart's De-light! O kin-dle, Lord, most ho-ly, Thy lamp with-in my breast, To do in spir-it low-ly All that may please Thee best.

entries.title: O Lord, I Am Not Worthy

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune NON DIGNUS (Traditional); words by From Landshuter Gesangbuch, 1777; translated by Anonymous.
entries.lyrics: O_ Lord, I am not wor-thy That_ Thou should'st come to me, But_ speak the words of com-fort, My spir-it healed shall be.

entries.title: O Lord of Heav'n and Earth and Sea
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ES IST KEIN TAG by Johann David Meyer (1636–1696); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: O Lord of_ Heav'n and_ earth_ and sea, To_ Thee all praise and glo-ry_ be; How_ shall we show our love to Thee, Who_ giv-est all?

entries.title: O Love, How Deep, How Broad, How High
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DEO GRACIAS (traditional English); words by Anonymous; translated by Benjamin Webb (1819–1885).
entries.lyrics: O love, how deep, how broad, how high, How pass_-ing thought_ and_ fan-ta-sy, That God, the Son_ of God, should take Our mor-tal form for mor-tals' sake!

entries.title: O Sacred Head, Now Wounded
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune PASSION CHORALE by Hans Leo Hassler (1564–1612); words by Bernard of Clairvaux (1091–1153); translated by James Waddel Alexander (1804–1859).
entries.lyrics: O sac-red Head, now wound-ed, with grief and shame_ weighed down, Now scorn-ful-ly sur-round-ed with thorns, Thine on_-ly crown; O sac_-red Head, what glo-ry, what bliss till now was Thine! Yet, though_ des-pised and gor-y, I joy to call Thee mine.

entries.title: O That the Lord Would Guide My Ways
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune EVAN by William Henry Havergal (1793–1870); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748).
entries.lyrics: O that the Lord would guide my ways To keep His sta-tutes still! O that my God would grant me grace To know and do His will!

entries.title: O Wondrous Type, O Vision Fair
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DEO GRACIAS (traditional English); words by Traditional Latin; translated by John Mason Neale (1818–1866).
entries.lyrics: O won-drous type! O vi-sion fair Of glo_-ry that_ the_ Church may share, Which Christ up-on_ the moun-tain shows, where bright-er than the sun He glows!

entries.title: Of the Father's Love Begotten (Divinum Mysterium, Isorythmic)
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DIVINUM MYSTERIUM (ISORYTHMIC) (traditional Latin); words by Aurelius Clemens Prudentius (348–413); translated by John Mason Neale (1818–1866) and Henry Williams Baker (1821–1877).
entries.lyrics: Of the Fa-ther's love be-got-ten Ere the worlds be-gan to be, He is Al-pha and O-me-ga, He the source, the end-ing He, Of the things that are, that have been, And that fu-ture years shall see, Ev-er-more and ev-er-more!

entries.title: Oh, Blest the House
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WO GOTT ZUM HAUS (From Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533); words by Christoph Karl Ludwig von Pfeil (1712–1784); translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: Oh blest the house, what-e'er be-fall, Where Je-sus Christ is All in All; Yea, if He were not dwell-ing there, How poor and dark and void_ it were!

entries.title: On Jordan's Bank the Baptist's Cry
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.

entries.lyrics: On Jor-dan's bank the Bap-tist's cry An-noun-ces that_ the Lord is nigh; Come, then, and hear-ken, for he brings Glad ti-dings from the King of kings!

entries.title: On My Heart Imprint Thine Image
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DER AM KREUZ by Johann Balthasar König (1691–1758); words by Thomas Hansen Kingo (1634–1703); translated by Peer Olsen Strømme (1856–1921).
entries.lyrics: On my heart im-print Thine_ i-mage, Bles-sed Je-sus, King of Grace That life's ri-ches, cares, and_ plea-sures, Have no pow'r to Thee ef-face; This the su-per-scrip-tion be: Je-sus cru-ci-fied for me, Is my life, my hope's foun-da-tion, And my glo-ry and sal-va-tion.

entries.title: On What Has Now Been Sown
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DARWALL by John Darwall (1731–1789); words by John Newton (1725–1807).
entries.lyrics: On what has now been sown Thy bless-ing, Lord, be-stow; The pow'r is Thine a-lone To make it spring and grow. Do Thou in grace the har-vest raise, And Thou a-lone shalt have the praise.

entries.title: Once in Royal David’s City

entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune IRBY by Henry John Gauntlett (1805–1876); words by Cecil Frances Alexander (1818–1895).
entries.lyrics: Once in roy-al Da_-vid’s_ cit-y Stood a low-ly cat_-tle_ shed, Where a moth-er laid_ her_ ba-by In a man-ger for_ His_ bed: Ma-ry was that moth-er mild, Je-sus Christ her lit_-tle_ child.

entries.title: Open Now Thy Gates of Beauty

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune UNSER HERRSCHER by Joachim Neander (1650–1680); words by Benjamin Schmolck (1672–1737); translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: Op-en now thy gates of beau-ty, Zi-on,_ let me en-ter there, Where my soul in joy-ful du-ty Waits for_ Him Who an-swers prayer. Oh, how bless-èd is this place, Filled with so-lace, light and grace!

entries.title: Over Kidron Jesus Treadeth
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune OVER KEDRON JESUS TRAEDER by Ludvig Mathias Lindeman (1812–1887); words by Thomas Hansen Kingo (1634–1703); translated by J. Jeffrey (19th century).
entries.lyrics: O-ver Kid-ron Je-sus tread-eth To His pas-sion for us all; Ev-ery hu-man eye be weep-ing, Tears of bit-ter grief let fall! Round His Spi-rit flock the foes, Place their shafts and bend their bows, Aim-ing at the Sav-ior sole-ly, While the world for-sakes Him_ whol-ly.

entries.title: Pass Me Not, O Gentle Saviour

entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune PASS ME NOT by William Howard Doane (1832–1915); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Pass me not, O gen-tle Sa-viour, Hear my hum-ble cry; While on o-thers Thou art call-ing, Do not pass me by. Sa-viour, Sa_-viour, Hear my hum-ble cry; While on o-thers Thou art call-ing, Do not pass me by.

entries.title: Praise God, from Whom All Blessings Flow (Doxology)
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune OLD HUNDREDTH by Louis Bourgeois (1510–1560); words by Thomas Ken (1637–1711).
entries.lyrics: Praise God, from whom all bless-ings flow; Praise Him, all crea-tures here be-low; Praise Him a-bove, ye heav’n-ly host; Praise Fa-ther, Son, and Ho-ly Ghost.

entries.title: Praise My Soul the King of Heaven
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune PRAISE MY SOUL by John Goss (1800–1880); words by Henry F. Lyte (1793–1847).
entries.lyrics: Praise, my soul, the King of hea-ven; To His feet thy tri-bute bring. Ran-somed, healed, re-stored, for-giv-en, Ev-er-more His pra-ises sing: A-lle-lu-ia! A-lle-lu-ia! Praise the ev-er-last-ing King.

entries.title: Praise the Lord, Ye Heavens Adore Him

entries.lyrics: Praise the Lord, ye heav'ns, a-dore_ Him; Praise Him, an-gels in the_ height. Sun and moon, re-joice be-fore_ Him; Praise Him, all ye stars of_ light. Praise the Lord,_ for He hath spo_-ken; Worlds His might-y voice o_-beyed. Laws which ne-ver shall be bro_-ken For their_ gui_-dance_ He hath_ made.

entries.title: Praise to the Lord, the Almighty
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score; every note and rhythm agrees with the score on Wikipedia's article.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune LOBE DEN HERREN (Stralsund Gesangbuch); words by Joachim Neander (1650–1680) and Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: Praise to the Lord, the Al-might-y, the King of cre-a-tion! O my soul, praise Him, for He is thy health and sal-va-tion! All ye who hear, Now to His tem-ple draw near; Praise Him in glad a-dor-a-tion.

entries.lyrics: Re-joice, O_ pil-grim throng! Re-joice, give_ thanks, and sing; Your fest-al_ ban-ner wave_ on_ high, The cross of Christ your King. Re-joice, re-joice, re-joice, Give_ thanks and sing.

entries.title: Rescue the Perishing

entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune RESCUE THE PERISHING by William Howard Doane (1832–1915); words by Fanny Jane Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Res-cue the per-ish-ing, care for the dy-ing, Snatch them in pi-ty from sin and the grave; Weep o'er the err-ing one, lift up the fall-en, Tell them of Je-sus, the might-y to save. Res-cue the per-ish-ing, care for the dy-ing, Je-sus is mer-ci-ful, Je-sus will save.

entries.title: Ride on! Ride on in Majesty
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WINCHESTER NEW (From "Musikalisches Handbuch", Hamburg, 1690); words by Henry Hart Milman (1791–1868).
entries.lyrics: Ride on! Ride on in ma-jes-ty! Hark! all the tribes ho-san-na cry; O Sa-vior meek pur-sue Thy road With palms and scat-tered gar-ments strewed.

entries.title: Savior, Like a Shepherd Lead Us
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune BRADBURY by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by Dorothy Ann Thrupp (1779–1847).
entries.lyrics: Sa-vior, like a shep-herd lead_ us,_ much we need Thy ten-der care; In Thy plea-sant pas-tures feed_ us,_ for our use Thy folds pre-pare. Bless-èd Je-sus, bless-èd Je-sus! Thou hast bought us, Thine we are. Bless-èd Je-sus, bless-èd Je-sus! Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

entries.title: Savior When in Dust to Thee
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ABERYSTWYTH (PARRY) by Joseph Parry (1841–1903); words by Robert Grant (1778–1838).
entries.lyrics: Sa-vior,_ when_ in dust to Thee Low we bow th'a-dor_-ing knee, When, re_-pent_-ant, to the skies Scarce we_ lift our weep-ing eyes, O by all the pains and_ woes Suff-ered once for man be_-low, Bend-ing from Thy throne on high, Hear our_ pen_-i-ten-tial cry!

entries.title: See Amid the Winter's Snow
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HUMILITY by John Goss (1800–1880); words by Edward Caswall (1814–1878).
entries.lyrics: See a-mid the win-ter's snow, Born for us on earth be-low, See, the gen-tle Lamb ap-pears, Pro-mised from e-ter-nal years. Hail that ev-er bles-sèd morn, Hail re-demp-tion's hap-py dawn, Sing through all Jer-u-sa-lem: Christ is born in Beth-le-hem.

entries.title: See, the Lord Ascends in Triumph
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune REX GLORIAE by Henry Thomas Smart (1813–1879); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: See, the Lord as-cends in tri-umph; see the King in_ ro-yal state, Ri-ding on the clouds, His char-iot, To His heav'n-ly pal-ace gate. Hark! the choirs of an-gel voi-ces Joy-ful al_-le-lu-ias sing, And the por-tals high are lift-ed To re-ceive their heav'n-ly King. Ho-ly Ghost, Il-lum-in-a-tor, shed Thy beams up-on_ our eyes, Help us to look up with Ste-phen, and to see be-yond_ the skies, Where the Son of Man in glo-ry Stand-ing is at God's_ right hand, Beck-'ning on His mar-tyr ar-my, suc-cor-ing His faith_-ful band.

entries.title: Silent Night
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune STILLE NACHT by Franz Xaver Gruber (1787–1863); words by Joseph Mohr (1792–1848) and John Freeman Young (1820–1885).
entries.lyrics: Si-lent night,_ ho-ly night,_ All is calm, all is bright, Round yon vir-gin moth-er and child._ Ho-ly in-fant so ten-der and mild, Sleep in heav-en-ly peace,_ Sleep in heav-en-ly peace._

entries.title: Sing, O Sing, This Blessed Morn
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune NATIVITY by William Henry Monk (1823–1889); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: Sing, O sing, this bless-ed morn, Un-to us a Child is born, Un-to us a Son is giv'n, God Him-self comes down from Heav'n. Sing, O sing, this bless-ed morn, Je-sus Christ to-day is born.

entries.title: Songs of Thankfulness and Praise
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. GEORGE by George Job Elvey (1816–1893); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: Songs of thank-ful-ness and praise, Je-sus, Lord, to Thee we raise, Man-i-fest-ed by the star To the sa-ges from a-far; Branch of ro-yal Da-vid's stem In Thy birth at Beth-le-hem; An-thems be to Thee add-ressed, God in man made man-i-fest.

entries.title: Souls of Men! Why Will Ye Scatter

The Com-fort-er has come, The Com-fort-er has come! The Ho-ly Ghost from heav'n, The Fa-ther's pro-mise giv'n; O spread the ti-dings 'round, Wher-ev-er man is found: The Com-fort-er has come!

In sor-row He's my com-fort, in trou-ble He's my stay; He_ tells me ev-ery care on Him to roll. He's the Li-ly of the Val-ley, the Bright and Morn-ing Star, He's the fair-est of ten thou-sand to my soul.

Oh love of God, how rich and pure!_ How meas-ure-less_ and strong! It shall for-ev-er-more en-dure,_ The saints' and an_-gels' song.

Are you rea-dy? Are you rea-dy? Are you rea-dy for the judg-ment day? Are you rea-dy? Are you rea-dy? For the judg-ment day?

An_-gels_ in bright rai-ment rolled the stone a-way, Kept_ the_ fold-ed grave-clothes where Thy_ bo-dy lay. Thine be the glo-ry, ri_-sen,_ con-qu’ring Son; End_-less_ is the vic-t’ry Thou o’er_ death hast won.

We mourn our grie-vous sin which hath_ Stirr'd the fire of Thy_ fierce wrath. Ho-ly and gra-cious God! Ho-ly and might-y God! Ho-ly and all‑ mer-ci-ful Sa_-vior! Thou e-ter-nal God! Save us, Lord, from sink_-ing In the deep and bit-ter flood. Ky-ri-e e-lei-son.

Praise the Lord, praise the Lord, Let the earth hear His voice! Praise the Lord, praise the Lord, Let the peo-ple re-joice! O come to the Fa-ther, through Je-sus the Son, And give Him the glor-y, great things He hath done!
